title: Pumcatawe
summary: Pumcatawe is recorded as a small tract of land and meadow east of Mastic River in Brookhaven. The name is connected with a Native person who formerly lived on the land.
history_content: The placename belongs to the Manor of St. George and Mastic River landscape. Dated patent and survey details appear in the Historic Timeline with source references.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Pumcatawe, Puncatane, Puncataue, Puencatame, and Punecatone. No separate linguistic translation is given; the name is treated as a personal name connected with someone who formerly lived on the land. Related personal-name forms include Pokkatone and Poquatone.

Why Place Names Matter

“Many place names have many stories explaining their origins, and to the extent that people believe those stories, they function as elements in the remembered histories of landscape.”

— William Cronon, Names on the Land: Place Names as Historical Evidence (2018), Section I, paragraph following the origin-stories discussion
preservation_content: Pumcatawe keeps a smaller named tract visible inside the larger Manor of St. George landscape, preserving evidence of Native personal names and remembered land use in colonial patent and survey records.
